name: Singapore Management University (Yong Pung How School of Law)
tech_center: Centre for Digital Law (consolidating the Centre for Computational Law and Centre for AI & Data Governance)
highlights: BSc (Computing & Law) — first of its kind in Singapore, jointly taught with the School of Computing and Information Systems
Centre for Computational Law's SGD 15M NRF programme built the open-source L4 domain-specific language for machine-executable contracts and statutes
SMU LIT hackathon — Singapore's largest inter-varsity legal tech hackathon, run in 2025 with Stanford CodeX and backed by the Ministry of Law and the Singapore Academy of Law
Partnership with the Future of Privacy Forum on digital law and data governance in APAC

name: National University of Singapore — Faculty of Law
tech_center: TRAIL — Centre for Technology, Robotics, Artificial Intelligence & the Law
highlights: Law, Algorithms and Artificial Intelligence course teaches practical statistics, machine learning, and NLP to lawyers
TRAIL's substantial scholarship includes 'Law and Technology in Singapore' and Simon Chesterman's AI governance work ('We, the Robots?')
Student-led Alt+Law club runs coding classes and hackathons (e.g., the NatashaBot chatbot for migrant workers); Rajah & Tann partnered on a seven-course tech programme for lawyers
LLM specialisation and graduate certificates in IP & Technology Law
caveats: Hands-on building is largely student-led; no established clinic where students build or deploy technology.

name: University of Hong Kong — Faculty of Law
tech_center: LITE Lab@HKU; Law and Technology Centre (joint with Computer Science since 2001, runs HKLII)
highlights: LITE Lab is explicitly experiential: credit-bearing courses (Tech Startup Law, Lawtech & Regtech Sandbox, LITE Internship) where students co-design and build lawtech tools with NGOs for access to justice
LLMs in Technology & IP Law and in Compliance & Regulation; AI law/ethics coursework
Law and Technology Centre built the 'HKU AI Lawyer' sentencing predictor; LITE Lab won a CLOC 2022 Legal Innovation award
Ecosystem ties to Cyberport, HK Science & Technology Park, and an advisory board including Ashurst, KWM, and Ant Group; Douglas Arner anchors globally prominent fintech/regtech scholarship

name: Chinese University of Hong Kong — Faculty of Law
tech_center: Centre for Legal Innovation and Digital Society (CLINDS)
highlights: New dedicated LLM in AI Law launching in the 2026-27 academic year
Legal Technologies courses at both undergraduate and postgraduate level; offerings on ODR, AI and IP, and smart contracts
Active research cluster (Jyh-An Lee on IP/AI/platforms) with annual AI governance conferences
caveats: Weaker on experiential, build-oriented training than HKU's LITE Lab; no clinic or hackathon identified.

name: Tsinghua University School of Law
tech_center: Institute for Studies on Artificial Intelligence and Law; Law and Big Data Research Center
highlights: China's flagship computational-law programme: a dedicated Juris Master in Computational Law (first cohort 2019, independent national admissions track since 2022) combining law with networks, big data, and AI coursework
Dean Shen Weixing is a leading computational-law scholar; annual International Forum on Computational Law
Applied research on big data and AI in China's smart-court/judicial informatization agenda
caveats: Experiential clinic details and student build opportunities are not well documented in public sources.

name: Peking University Law School
tech_center: PKU Legal AI Laboratory (2017, with Gridsum); Digital Rule of Law Research Center
highlights: Early mover: Legal AI Lab founded in 2017 for AI product R&D in legal applications
Courses in Law and Artificial Intelligence, Topics in Digital Law, and Data Regulation and Compliance
Active digital-law scholarship and conferences on AI and legal theory
caveats: The Legal AI Lab's current vitality is uncertain; no legal-tech degree, build clinic, or hackathon identified.

name: Hebrew University of Jerusalem — Faculty of Law
tech_center: Federmann Cyber Security Research Center — Cyber Law Program (joint with the Benin School of Computer Science)
highlights: Deep cyber/tech course cluster: Cyber Law, Israeli and International Cybersecurity Law, Cyber Crimes, Internet Governance, plus cross-listed CS courses
Year-long Clinic on Digital Rights and Human Rights in Cyberspace within one of Israel's leading clinical programs
Federmann Center scholarship spans cyber operations law, cybercrime, and AI governance, with government (INCD) ties
caveats: Strength is cyber and security law rather than hands-on legal-tech tooling; no build labs or hackathons found.

name: Tel Aviv University — Buchmann Faculty of Law
tech_center: Shamgar Center for Digital Law and Innovation (2022); Algorithmic Governance Lab
highlights: Law & Technology specialization in the Parasol Foundation International LLM (14-15 of 32 credits in tech-law courses)
Israel's first Privacy Clinic (with the Shamgar Center since 2022)
Top-tier faculty: Niva Elkin-Koren (AI governance, platform regulation), Michael Birnhack (privacy/data protection); dedicated 2025 journal volume on AI
Algorithmic Governance Lab cooperates with government and industry

name: Reichman University — Harry Radzyner Law School
tech_center: Zvi Meitar Institute for Legal Implications of Emerging Technologies
highlights: MA/LLM in Law, Technology and Business Innovation (200+ students, running since ~2020)
Selective cross-disciplinary Zvi Meitar Emerging Technologies Program spanning Law, Business, CS, and Government schools
Institute policy work on responsible AI regulation; strong university-wide entrepreneurship culture
caveats: Weaker on hands-on build-and-deploy legal tech; no dedicated legal-tech clinic verified.

name: National Law School of India University (NLSIU)
tech_center: JSW Centre for the Future of Law (2024)
highlights: 'Law and New Technologies' built into the core curriculum, with AI and the Future of Law and AI Governance & Ethics electives anchored by the JSW Centre
Students get access to premium AI tools plus AI skills workshops; full-time JSW-CFL internship programme
L-Tech (est. 1995) is India's oldest student tech-law society; LLM concentration covers comparative AI regulation including the EU AI Act
caveats: Capacity is new (2024-); no build-oriented clinic or legal-tech hackathon yet evident.

name: NALSAR University of Law
tech_center: Centre for Law and AI; Centre for Cyber Laws and Forensic Sciences
highlights: NPTEL/SWAYAM MOOC 'Artificial Intelligence, Law and Justice' has reached 10,000+ learners
NSDC-certified Diploma in Future of Law: AI, Technology & Legal Practice (with LawSikho, 2025); one-year Advanced Diploma in Cyber Laws
Active student scholarship via the Tech Law Forum
caveats: Strength is distance/professional education and MOOCs more than on-campus build-focused legal tech.

name: O.P. Jindal Global University (Jindal Global Law School)
tech_center: Cyril Shroff Centre for AI, Law & Regulation (India's first dedicated AI-law centre, ₹15 crore endowment); JIRICO
highlights: LLM in Artificial Intelligence and Emerging Technologies — a 12-month blended programme, first of its kind in India — plus an LLM in IP & Technology Law
Cyril Shroff Centre plans partnerships with NITI Aayog, MeitY, RBI, SEBI, TRAI, and global bodies (OECD, US FTC, UK AISI)
Annual Jindal Technology Law and Policy International Moot; Qualcomm-funded IP-competition research via JIRICO
caveats: Practical build-oriented legal-tech training is still limited; centre work is research and policy oriented.
